title: Paper Bag Detective
objective: Describe the observable properties of a paper bag and choose its safe use or handling.
introduction: Milo examines a paper bag: what can Maxine observe, and how can she handle it safely?

items.prompt: Maxine gently bends a rubber band, spoon, stone, and mirror. Which material is flexible?
items.explanation: A rubber band bends and returns to shape, so it is flexible. Metal, stone, and glass resist bending or can break.

items.prompt: Milo wipes a spill with a jar, ruler, cloth, and mirror. Which absorbs water?
items.explanation: Cotton cloth has fibers that soak up water. Glass and mirrors repel water, and a ruler absorbs much less.

items.prompt: Milo presses a rubber ball, foil, sponge, and metal nail. Which material is hard?
items.explanation: A metal nail stays firm and resists bending, showing hardness. A ball, foil, and sponge are softer or more flexible.

items.prompt: Maxine carries a paper bag with a light book. What property should she remember?
items.explanation: A paper bag can tear when pulled too hard, so tears easily is an important property to remember.

items.prompt: Before studying a paper bag, which action is safe?

options.text: Look at it and touch it gently

items.explanation: Looking and gentle touching allow a safe observation. Tasting, throwing, or soaking the bag are unsafe choices.
